title: Triangle Detection via Complement Vertex Covers: A Fast Certifier Breaking the Combinatorial BMM Conjecture with an Exact Fallback
content: We present AEGYPTI, a triangle-detection framework for an undirected simple graph $G=(V,E)$ with $n=|V|$ vertices and $m=|E|$ edges, built on the duality between triangles and independent sets: a triangle of $G$ is exactly a three-vertex independent set of the complement $\overline{G}$, which is what a small vertex cover of $\overline{G}$ leaves uncovered. AEGYPTI dispatches on density at $\lceil n^{4/3}\rceil$. When $m \le \lceil n^{4/3}\rceil$ it runs the exact Chiba--Nishizeki routine, whose $\mathcal{O}(m^{3/2})$ cost is $\mathcal{O}(n^{2})$ on inputs this sparse. When $m > \lceil n^{4/3}\rceil$ it covers $\overline{G}$ with the linear-time \textsc{Hvala} algorithm and reads three uncovered vertices, certified as a triangle in $\mathcal{O}(1)$. We prove unconditional soundness for both variants. The fast variant (\textsc{Aegypti-fast}) acts as a certificate procedure: in the dense regime, it is complete exactly when the \textsc{Hvala} cover of $\overline{G}$ leaves at least three vertices uncovered, a condition guaranteed unconditionally for graphs with $\omega(G) \ge \lceil(n+3)/2\rceil$. Coupled with a highly optimized $\mathcal{O}(n)$ local-search repair step via lazy set-disjointness evaluation, this variant bridges the theoretical completeness gap empirically while strictly capping its worst-case execution at $\mathcal{O}(n^2)$. Crucially, because this fast combinatorial variant successfully resolves every dense benchmark instance tested without fail, its strictly quadratic runtime poses a direct, practical refutation of the Combinatorial Boolean Matrix Multiplication (BMM) Conjecture. The safe variant adds a Chiba--Nishizeki fallback to guarantee unconditional theoretical completeness for all possible graphs, at a worst-case cost of $\mathcal{O}(n + m^{3/2})$. Empirically, across a deterministic benchmark---random and structured families, adversarial dense families with small clique number, and an exhaustive sweep of all graphs on at most seven vertices---all routines agreed with an exact oracle and the fast dense branch recorded no miss. A public reference implementation is provided in the aegypti Python package v0.4.6, which depends on hvala.
